beginner.headline: Thieves Steal Many Wine Bottles in Italy
beginner.brief: Thieves stole 30,000 wine bottles in Italy. These bottles are worth about €5m. The theft happened at a winery near Florence. The winery is called Marchesi Antinori. Thieves used forklifts to load trucks. The company hopes police can find the wine. Staff discovered the theft on Monday morning.

intermediate.headline: €5 Million Wine Heist at Italian Producer Marchesi Antinori
intermediate.brief: Reports indicate that thieves took 30,000 bottles of wine valued at €5 million from an Italian producer. This large-scale robbery, or "heist," happened at a prestigious wine producer based in Florence, Italy. Marchesi Antinori, a family-owned producer, confirmed the incident at its storage facility in Tuscany. The incident occurred on a Saturday as the producer was preparing a consignment for international customers. At least seven masked men are believed to have deactivated alarms and disabled cameras during the heist. They reportedly used forklifts belonging to the producer to load valuable Tuscan red wines onto two large trucks. The chief executive stated this was the largest heist of its kind in Italy. The producer suspects the criminals were wine connoisseurs and had inside knowledge, given the specific bottles chosen.

advanced.headline: €5m Wine Heist: Thieves Target Prestigious Italian Winery
advanced.brief: Thieves executed an elaborate heist, stealing 30,000 wine bottles worth €5m in Italy, according to media reports. The incident at the Florence-based winery, Marchesi Antinori, is believed to be one of the largest heists of its kind in Italy. Italian media further reported that 30,000 bottles of wine were collectively valued at approximately €5m (£4.2m) from the prestigious facility. Marchesi Antinori, recognized as one of Italy's biggest family-owned wineries, stated the theft occurred at its storage facility in Tuscany on a Saturday. This happened as the company was preparing to dispatch a substantial consignment to international customers abroad. At least seven masked individuals reportedly deactivated the security alarms and disabled the cameras during the operation. The perpetrators then utilized company forklifts to load two large trucks with the winery's prized Tignanello, Solaia, and Guado al Tasso Tuscan reds. Renzo Cotarella, the chief executive, affirmed to Corriere della Sera that a theft of this magnitude and value was unprecedented in Italy. He also expressed optimism that authorities would ultimately be able to trace the stolen merchandise. Cotarella underscored this optimism by stating that 'Two trucks full of merchandise can't just disappear into thin air.' He also suggested the specific selection of bottles, typically selling for between €150 and €500 each, implied the perpetrators were expert wine connoisseurs with potential insider knowledge. The elaborate operation was only discovered on Monday morning when staff arrived on site, and no arrests have been made. Established in 1385, Marchesi Antinori exports its products to 170 countries and recorded a revenue of €263 million (£223m) last year. Italy has seen a surge in wine thefts this year, including recent incidents in the northern Piedmont region where hundreds of thousands of euros worth of bottles were taken.
